arxiv-2104-02301.title: Hyperspectral and LiDAR data classification based on linear self-attention Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Key Research and Development Program of China under Grant 2018AAA0100602, in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant U1706218, and in part b
arxiv-2104-02301.creator: Min Feng, Feng Gao, Jian Fang, Junyu Dong
arxiv-2104-02301.description: Abstract In this paper, an efficient linear self-attention fusion model is proposed for the task of hyperspectral image (HSI) and LiDAR data joint classification. The proposed method is comprised of a feature extraction module, an attention module, and a fusion module. The attention module is a plug-and-play linear self-attention module that can be extensively used in any model.

arxiv-2111-15440.title: Effects on the local dark matter distribution due to the Large Magellanic Cloud 2021 Effects on the local dark matter distribution due to the Large Magellanic Cloud – References
arxiv-2111-15440.creator: Katelin Donaldson, Michael S. Petersen, Jorge Peñarrubia
arxiv-2111-15440.description: Abstract We study the local dark matter distribution in two models for the Milky Way (MW)-Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) interaction. The effect of the LMC on the local dark matter distribution is dependent on the evolution of the MW-LMC system, such that a static model is insufficient to accurately model the dark matter velocity distribution in the solar neighbourhood.

arxiv-2206-07866.title: Resonant Axion Radiation Conversion in Solar Spicules
arxiv-2206-07866.creator: Aiichi Iwazaki
arxiv-2206-07866.description: Abstract It has recently been observed that solar spicules covering almost of all solar surface have strong magnetic field B ∼ 10 2 B\sim 10^{2} G. They are supposed to be plasma jets emitted from chromosphere and they arrive up to ∼ 10 4 \sim 10^{4} km.

arxiv-2210-04978.title: Discrete homogeneity and ends of manifolds
arxiv-2210-04978.creator: Vitalij A. Chatyrko and Alexandre Karassev
arxiv-2210-04978.description: Abstract . It is shown that a connected non-compact metrizable manifold of dimension ≥ 2 \geq 2 is strongly discrete homogeneous if and only if it has one end (in the sense of Freudenthal compactification). 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 57S05; Secondary 54F15, 54D35 1. Introduction All spaces are assumed to be metrizable, and all maps continuous.

arxiv-2301-00937.title: FEASTS: IGM cooling triggered by tidal interactions through the diffuse HI phase around NGC 4631 Facilities: FAST, GALEX, Spitzer, WSRT Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , Astrosclicer ( Punzo et al. 2017 ) , BAYGAUD
arxiv-2301-00937.creator: Jing Wang (王菁), Dong Yang (杨冬), S-H. Oh, Lister Staveley-Smith, Jie Wang, Q. Daniel Wang, Kelley M. Hess, Luis C. Ho, Ligang Hou, Yingjie Jing, Peter Kamphuis, Fujia Li, Xuchen Lin (林旭辰), Ziming Liu, Li Shao, Shun Wang (王舜), Ming Zhu
arxiv-2301-00937.description: Abstract We use the single-dish radio telescope FAST to map the H ​ i {\rm H}{\textsc{i}} in the tidally interacting NGC 4631 group with a resolution of 3.24 ′ (7 kpc), reaching a 5- σ \sigma column density limit of 10 17.9 ​ cm − 2 10^{17.9}~\rm{cm^{-2}} assuming a line width of 20 km ​ s − 1 \rm{km~s^{-1}} .

arxiv-2310-04870.title: Lemur: Integrating Large Language Models in Automated Program Verification
arxiv-2310-04870.creator: Haoze Wu, Clark Barrett, Nina Narodytska
arxiv-2310-04870.description: Abstract The demonstrated code-understanding capability of LLMs raises the question of whether they can be used for automated program verification, a task that demands high-level abstract reasoning about program properties that is challenging for verification tools. We propose a general methodology to combine the power of LLMs and automated reasoners for automated program verification.

arxiv-2401-10759.title: Interactions with Prompt Problems: A New Way to Teach Programming with Large Language Models Conference: CHI Conference on Computer-Human Interaction; CHI Conference on Computer-Human Interaction ; DOI: 11.1111/1111111.1111111 ISBN: 111-1-111-1111-1/11/11 CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer
arxiv-2401-10759.creator: James Prather, Paul Denny, Juho Leinonen, David H. Smith IV, Brent N. Reeves, Stephen MacNeil, Brett A. Becker, Andrew Luxton-Reilly, Thezyrie Amarouche, Bailey Kimmel
arxiv-2401-10759.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) have upended decades of pedagogy in computing education. Students previously learned to code through writing many small problems with less emphasis on code reading and comprehension . Recent research has shown that free code generation tools powered by LLMs can solve introductory programming problems presented in natural language with ease.

arxiv-2407-15606.title: Power counting of the pion-dilaton effective field theory
arxiv-2407-15606.creator: Maarten Golterman
arxiv-2407-15606.description: Abstract Confining QCD-like theories close to the conformal window have a “walking” coupling. This is believed to lead to a light singlet scalar meson in the low-energy spectrum, a dilaton, which is the pseudo Nambu–Goldstone boson for the approximate scale symmetry.

arxiv-2412-20763.title: Realizing modular data from centers of near-group categories
arxiv-2412-20763.creator: Zhiqiang Yu 1, Qing Zhang 2
arxiv-2412-20763.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhiqiang Yu 1, Qing Zhang 2. In this paper, we show the existence of a near-group category of type ℤ / 4 ​ ℤ × ℤ / 4 ​ ℤ + 16 \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}+16 and compute the modular data of its Drinfeld center.

arxiv-2501-08074.title: Artificial Liver Classifier: A New Alternative to Conventional Machine Learning Models
arxiv-2501-08074.creator: Mahmood A. Jumaah, Yossra H. Ali, Tarik A. Rashid
arxiv-2501-08074.description: Abstract Supervised machine learning classifiers sometimes face challenges related to the performance, accuracy, or overfitting. This paper introduces the Artificial Liver Classifier (ALC), a novel supervised learning model inspired by the human liver’s detoxification function. The ALC is characterized by its simplicity, speed, capability to reduce overfitting, and effectiveness in addressing multi-class classification problems through straightforward mathematical operations.

arxiv-2504-00273.title: A weak entanglement approximation for nuclear structure: a progress report
arxiv-2504-00273.creator: Calvin W. Johnson, Oliver C. Gorton
arxiv-2504-00273.description: Abstract We report on a recently proposed approach, inspired by quantum information theory, for calculating low-energy nuclear structure in the framework of the configuration-interaction shell-model. Empirical evidence has demonstrated that the many-proton and many-neutron partitions of nuclear configuration-interaction wave functions are weakly entangled, especially away from N = Z N=Z .

arxiv-2510-09211.title: DICE: Structured Reasoning in LLMs through SLM-Guided Chain-of-Thought Correction
arxiv-2510-09211.creator: Yiqi Li, Yusheng Liao, Zhe Chen, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang
arxiv-2510-09211.description: Abstract When performing reasoning tasks with user-specific requirements, such as strict output formats, large language models (LLMs) often prioritize reasoning over adherence to detailed instructions. Fine-tuning LLMs on supervised datasets to address this is impractical due to high computational costs and limited parameter access.

arxiv-2511-20181.title: High order tracer variance stable transport with low order energy conserving dynamics for the thermal shallow water equations
arxiv-2511-20181.creator: David Lee, Kieran Ricardo, Tamara Tambyah
arxiv-2511-20181.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by David Lee, Kieran Ricardo, Tamara Tambyah. A high order discontinuous Galerkin method for the material transport of thermodynamic tracers is coupled to a low order mixed finite element solver in the context of the thermal shallow water equations. The coupling preserves the energy conserving structure of the low order dynamics solver, while the high order material transport scheme is provably tracer variance conserving, or damping with the inclusion of upwinding.

europmc-pmc6544318.title: Microstructural and functional gradients are increasingly dissociated in transmodal cortices.
europmc-pmc6544318.creator: Paquola C, Vos De Wael R, Wagstyl K, Bethlehem RAI, Hong SJ, Seidlitz J, Bullmore ET, Evans AC, Misic B, Margulies DS, Smallwood J, Bernhardt BC.
europmc-pmc6544318.description: While the role of cortical microstructure in organising neural function is well established, it remains unclear how structural constraints can give rise to more flexible elements of cognition. While nonhuman primate research has demonstrated a close structure-function...

pmc-11603366.title: A lightweight deep learning method to identify different types of cervical cancer
pmc-11603366.creator: Md Humaion Kabir Mehedi, Moumita Khandaker, Shaneen Ara, Md Ashraful Alam, M F Mridha, Zeyar Aung
pmc-11603366.description: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer in women’s bodies after breast cancer. Cervical cancer develops from dysplasia or cervical intraepithelial neoplasm (CIN), the early stage of the disease, and is characterized by the aberrant growth of cells in the cervix lining. It is primarily caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection, which spreads through sexual activity.

pmc-11879325.title: Onlay mesh versus suture repair for smaller umbilical hernias in adults—early results from SUMMER trial: randomized clinical trial
pmc-11879325.creator: Mathias Bergström, Björn Widhe, Gabriel Granåsen, Anna Löf Granström, Johan Ohlsson, Simone Schult, Ursula Dahlstrand, Johanna Österberg, Peter Loogna, Sven Bringman, Maria Melkemichel
pmc-11879325.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMesh repair is recommended for umbilical hernias larger than 1 cm to reduce recurrence rates, yet current evidence remains limited for smaller umbilical hernias. Important questions concern optimal mesh positioning and wound complications/surgical-site occurrences.

pmc-12472907.title: Prospective Observational Case Series in Infertile Women with Overweight or Obesity Treated with a Very-Low Calorie Ketogenic Diet (VLCKD) Prior to an In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) Treatment
pmc-12472907.creator: Maíra Casalechi, Alessandra Piontini, Annaelisa Nicolosi, Francesca Bergomas, Filomena Napolitano, Stefano Turolo, Marco Reschini, Alessandra Riccaboni, Roberta Bellinghieri, Edgardo Somigliana, Luisella Vigna
pmc-12472907.description: Background: Elevated BMI in women is linked to metabolic and endocrine imbalances that impair fertility and increase pregnancy risks. While >10% weight loss before an Assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment may improve outcomes, sustained results through conventional diets are challenging. A very-low calorie ketogenic diet (VLCKD) promotes rapid fat loss while preserving lean mass and may offer long-term benefits.

pmc-12528378.title: The effect of the use of irrigation activation methods with different file systems on the amount of apical debris extrusion
pmc-12528378.creator: Seden Kara Ongun, Oğuz Tavşan
pmc-12528378.description: This study evaluated apical debris extrusion caused by passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI), sonic activation (SA) and conventional irrigation (CI) in combination with different file systems. A total of 135 extracted human mandibular premolar teeth were used. The samples were divided into nine groups (n = 15) based on three main irrigation activation techniques and three subgroups of file systems.

pmc-12549766.title: Forecasting age-standardized incidence rates of gastric cancer from 1990–2050 in Japan according to H. pylori prevalence and eradication scenarios
pmc-12549766.creator: Byron Sigel, Eiko Saito, Daisuke Yoneoka, Tomohiro Matsuda, Kota Katanoda
pmc-12549766.description: BackgroundThis study examines the influence of H. pylori eradication policies on gastric cancer incidence rates in Japan utilizing nationally representative registry data. It evaluates the impact of the H. pylori eradication policies introduced in 2000 and 2013, along with future eradication scenarios, on age-standardized gastric cancer rates.

pmc-12564305.title: Role of the Inflammasome Pathway According to the Expression of Proteins and Genetic Polymorphisms in COVID-19 Patients
pmc-12564305.creator: Thiago Rodrigues dos Santos, Lucas Baena Carstens, Leonardo Vinícius Barbosa, Mariana Collete, Natan de Araujo, Caroline Busatta Vaz de Paula, Marina Luise Viola Azevedo, Ana Clara de Almeida, Seigo Nagashima, Lucia de Noronha, Cleber Machado-Souza, Chiara Colarusso, Rosalinda Sorrentino
pmc-12564305.description: COVID-19 severity is frequently linked to exacerbated inflammation, with the inflammasome pathway playing a key role in activating inflammatory interleukins. This observational post-mortem study evaluated the expression of inflammasome-associated molecules in patients who died from COVID-19 during the second wave. Minimally invasive autopsies were performed on patients from the first (n = 24) and second (n = 18) waves.

pmc-12606201.title: The efficiency and safety of low-dose intravenous indomethacin for closure of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm neonate: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12606201.creator: Wasana Hongkan, Narueporn Petarwut, Thanatda Siriporn, Nirucha Thamwiriyakul, Tharathorn Durongbhandhu
pmc-12606201.description: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is a common complication in prematurity. Intravenous indomethacin, three doses, is an effective medication for closure PDA, but complications about renal impairment and gastrointestinal (GI) problems should be considered. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of low-dose intravenous indomethacin (two doses) with the conventional three-dose for the closure of PDA in preterm neonates.

pmc-12729209.title: The association between sedentary behavior and infertility: a population-based cross-sectional observational study and Mendelian randomization analysis
pmc-12729209.creator: Yun Wang, Hongchu Bao, Zhenteng Liu, Qinglan Qu, Dongmei Zhao, Shunzhi He
pmc-12729209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThe relationship between sedentary behavior and infertility remains ambiguous and contentious. This study seeks to elucidate this association by analyzing data from the 2013–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), coupled with Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses.MethodsOur analysis comprised 2904 female participants, aged 20 to 49 years, enrolled in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) during the 2013–2018 cycles.

pmc-13146061.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2085 STROKE RISK AND ITS ASSOCIATED FACTORS AMONG HEALTHCARE WORKERS: USING THE STROKE RISKOMETER APP: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
pmc-13146061.creator: Tasneem M Mansy, Ibrahim Y Ibrahim, Gannatallah A Mahmoud, Dalia H Mohamed, Ahmed A Mohamed, Mohamad A Sakr, Mostafa Mahran
pmc-13146061.description: Background and aimsStroke is the second cause of mortality and the third cause of disability worldwide. Main controllable risks include hypertension, diabetes, smoking, obesity, and physical inactivity. Nonetheless, the evidence of stroke risk among healthcare professionals in Egypt remains limited.

pmc-13540935.creator: Victor M Cnossen, Olivia A C Lamers, Rogier P van Leeuwen, Paul Zimmer-Harwood, Meta Roestenberg, Ingrid M C Kamerling, Marie-Astrid Hoogerwerf

pmc-13548258.title: Experiences of pregnant women staying in a maternity waiting home at Ari zone public health facilities, Ethiopia: a phenomenological qualitative study
pmc-13548258.creator: Worku Mimani Minuta, Abera Gezume, Ermias Wabeto Wana, Getamesay Aynalem Tesfaye, Getachew Nigussie Bolado
pmc-13548258.description: AbstractBackgroundMaternity Waiting Homes (MWHs) are a key strategy for improving maternal health by bringing expectant women closer to health facilities and skilled birth attendants. Despite their potential benefits, a woman’s stay is shaped by various factors, including emotional, social and logistical aspects.

pmc-13583826.title: Development of a core outcome set for the evaluation of shared decision-making interventions in healthcare: a study protocol
pmc-13583826.creator: Christin Hoffmann, Joanne E Butterworth, Florian Naye, Maureen Smith, Taona Nyamapfene, Samuel Lawday, Kerry Avery, Hilary Bekker, Paulina Bravo, Simon Décary, Adrian Edwards, Glyn Elwyn, Ellen G Engelhardt, Juan Victor Ariel Franco, Mirjam M Garvelink, Anik MC Giguere, Martin Härter, Tammy Hoffmann
pmc-13583826.description: IntroductionShared decision-making (SDM) is a process whereby patients are supported to reach decisions about their healthcare in collaboration with healthcare professionals. Despite decades of SDM research, the impact of using SDM interventions (eg, patient decision aids, decision coaching, question prompt lists, training and feedback or service changes) on clinical and health service outcomes remains uncertain.

pmc-13598930.title: An institutional experience of a scripting‐driven automation of the emergent palliative radiotherapy workflow
pmc-13598930.creator: Shadab Momin, Eduard Schreibmann, Justin Roper, Beth Ghavidel, Maxine Washington, Oluwatosin Kayode, Pretesh Patel, Ashish Patel, Hania Al‐Hallaq, Yulia Lyatskaya
